document:
Exercise: Lying Cambered Barbell Row

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
isolation

Force Type:
pull

Difficulty Level:
beginner

Movement Patterns:

- unilateral_rowing

Primary Muscles:

- middle back

Secondary Muscles:

- biceps
- lats
- traps

Equipment:

- barbell

Fatigue Score:
3

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
0.8

Energy Requirement:
moderate

Recovery Time:
24 hours

Goals:

- improve_overall_upper_body_pulling_ability
- develop_strength_in_the_middle_back_muscles

Contraindications:

- condition: shoulder injury, reason: The exercise can put strain on the shoulder joint and rotator cuff muscles.
- condition: lower back pain, reason: Improper form or excessive weight may exacerbate lower back issues.

Exercise Variations:

- name: Incline Lying Cambered Barbell Row, instructions: ['Place a cambered bar underneath an incline exercise bench.', 'Lie face down on the incline exercise bench and grab the bar using a palms down (pronated grip) that is wider than shoulder width. This will be your starting position.', 'As you exhale row the bar up as you keep the elbows close to your body to either your chest, in order to target the upper mid back, or to your stomach if targeting the lats is your goal.', 'After a second hold at the top, lower back down to the starting position slowly as you inhale.']

Substitution Options:

- exercise_name: Seated Cable Row, equipment: cable machine
- exercise_name: T-Bar Row, equipment: T-bar attachment and rack

Instructions:

- Place a cambered bar underneath an exercise bench.
- Lie face down on the exercise bench and grab the bar using a palms down (pronated grip) that is wider than shoulder width. This will be your starting position.
- As you exhale row the bar up as you keep the elbows close to your body to either your chest, in order to target the upper mid back, or to your stomach if targeting the lats is your goal.
- After a second hold at the top, lower back down to the starting position slowly as you inhale.
